**6B.1 Research Note: Narendra Modi (2024)**

**Bottom line**
The evidence is mixed, but the stronger reading is **partial yes, not a clean yes**. Modi’s 2024 government did produce several real welfare-oriented actions: a tightly managed budget with high capital expenditure, expansion of health and agriculture infrastructure, rural and women-focused schemes, and some administrative modernization. But a large share of the record still looks **politically instrumentalized**: communal campaign rhetoric, targeted transfer politics after the election setback, opaque patronage-linked finance, and serious failures to protect vulnerable communities in Manipur and Jammu and Kashmir. So welfare was present as a governing goal, but not consistently above propaganda, patronage, or political management.

**Accepted Claims**

- **Title:** Interim budget prioritized disadvantaged groups while staying fiscally restrained  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 1 Feb 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-finance-minister-unveils-budget-with-focus-on-poor-women-youth-and-farmers/1948406/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported that the budget explicitly centered the poor, women, youth, and farmers, while resisting a giveaway structure and keeping fiscal discipline. This is the cleanest early-2024 signal that welfare was treated as a serious policy objective rather than pure electioneering.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 5B.10

- **Title:** Government resisted pre-election populism and kept fiscal consolidation  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 1 Feb 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/economy/india-refrains-from-populist-budget-before-election-trims-fiscal-deficit/1948823/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters said the administration avoided a classic pre-poll giveaway budget and stuck to deficit reduction. That supports a reading of rule-based economic stewardship, not just patronage or short-term propaganda spending.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 5B.10

- **Title:** Strong FY24 growth created fiscal room for welfare and investment  
  **Publisher:** Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation / PIB  
  **Date:** 31 May 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2022323&lang=2&reg=3  
  **Claim summary:** The government’s own release reported 8.2% real GDP growth in FY 2023-24 and 7.8% in Q4. This does not prove welfare intent, but it supports the argument that the government had resources and macro space to pursue broader public purposes.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 5B.10

- **Title:** Administration set explicit long-run welfare and livelihood targets  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via The Straits Times  
  **Date:** 8 May 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/indias-modi-chasing-reform-legacy-shifts-income-goals-for-struggling-farmers  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported targets to lift rural incomes, expand non-farm jobs, and increase agricultural investment. This is direct evidence that the government was not framing welfare only as handouts, but also as livelihood transformation.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 5B.10

- **Title:** Post-election budget shifted money toward jobs and rural programs  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 23 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/india-focuses-on-job-creation-rural-areas-in-first-budget-after-election/2186863/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported that the first post-election budget kept jobs and rural spending high, alongside higher education loans and manufacturing incentives. That is real welfare content, though it was clearly shaped by the electoral setback.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 5B.10

- **Title:** Budget preserved capex while redirecting spending to jobs and rural demand  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 23 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/india-budget-shifts-spending-priorities-while-keeping-fiscal-deficit-in-check/2187377/  
  **Claim summary:** The budget cut the fiscal-deficit target to 4.9% of GDP while raising capital and investment-linked spending. This is the best evidence that welfare and growth were treated as governing priorities, not merely rhetorical cover.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 5B.10

- **Title:** Health, education, and digital public infrastructure expanded in the first 100 days  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare  
  **Date:** 28 Sep 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=153215&lang=1&reg=3  
  **Claim summary:** The government highlighted expanded Ayushman Bharat coverage for seniors, U-WIN, new medical seats, and digital health registries. This is strong welfare evidence, though it is official self-reporting and not independent validation of outcomes.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1

- **Title:** Digital health infrastructure expanded at scale  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare  
  **Date:** 17 Dec 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2085201&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** ABDM reportedly built large-scale digital health infrastructure, including ABHA accounts and linked health records. This supports a view that welfare was being operationalized through state capacity, not just through slogans.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1

- **Title:** Digital Agriculture Mission aimed at productivity and farmer support  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare  
  **Date:** 2 Sep 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2050966&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The mission used digital public infrastructure, crop estimation, and data-driven support for farmers. That is substantive welfare-adjacent governance, especially for a large vulnerable constituency.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 5B.10

- **Title:** Rural women were mobilized into SHGs at very large scale  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Rural Development  
  **Date:** 30 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2039162&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The ministry said DAY-NRLM had mobilized more than 10 crore women into self-help groups. This is a meaningful pro-welfare distribution claim, especially for poorer rural women, though it remains official self-reporting.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1

- **Title:** Minority-women empowerment and welfare schemes continued  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Minority Affairs  
  **Date:** 11 Dec 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2083334&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The government said PM VIKAS/Nai Roshni trained about 4.35 lakh minority women and emphasized rights, literacy, and leadership. This is useful positive welfare evidence, though it also functions as political credit-claiming.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 2B.6

- **Title:** Manipur relief package and displaced-person support  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Home Affairs  
  **Date:** 17 Jun 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2025980&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The Home Ministry said it was committed to safety for citizens in Manipur and outlined forces, strict action, and support for food, water, medicine, education, and rehabilitation. This is genuine welfare-and-protection language, but it was reactive rather than preventative.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 3B.1

**Counterevidence**

- **Title:** Modi’s campaign used communal scapegoating instead of welfare-centered public purpose  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 23 Apr 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-calls-rivals-pro-muslim-as-election-campaign-changes-tack/2053223/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported Modi called Muslims “infiltrators” and linked them to wealth redistribution fears. That is strong evidence that a lot of political messaging was grievance-driven propaganda rather than welfare-centered governance.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 2B.6

- **Title:** Election Commission censured communal campaigning  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 22 May 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-poll-panel-orders-modis-bjp-opposition-congress-to-show-restraint-in-campaign/2096809/  
  **Claim summary:** The EC told BJP campaigners to stop communal campaigning after complaints about divisive speech, including Modi’s remarks. This supports the view that political mobilization often displaced welfare concerns.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 2B.6

- **Title:** Human Rights Watch said the campaign normalized hate speech and intimidation  
  **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  **Date:** 14 Aug 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/14/india-hate-speech-fueled-modis-election-campaign  
  **Claim summary:** HRW described the campaign as using hate speech against Muslims and other minorities, and as normalizing intimidation and discrimination. That strongly undercuts the claim that welfare was the core governing purpose.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 2B.6, 3B.1

- **Title:** Manipur violence was not effectively stopped  
  **Publisher:** Amnesty International  
  **Date:** 16 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/india-authorities-missing-in-action-amid-ongoing-violence-and-impunity-in-manipur-state-new-testimonies/  
  **Claim summary:** Amnesty said state and central authorities failed to end the violence, protect displaced residents, or hold vigilante groups accountable. That is direct counterevidence to a welfare-first reading.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 3B.1

- **Title:** Jammu and Kashmir abuses continued with little accountability  
  **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  **Date:** 31 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/31/india-repression-persists-jammu-and-kashmir  
  **Claim summary:** HRW said security forces continued arbitrary detention, extrajudicial killings, and other abuses with little accountability. This suggests welfare and protection were secondary to coercive state control in at least some domains.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 3B.1

- **Title:** Post-election budget became coalition and vote-retention politics  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 23 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters said the budget devoted large sums to jobs, rural programs, and coalition states to win back voters and retain support. This is welfare spending, but it is also explicit patronage logic.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 5B.10

- **Title:** Opaque political finance favored the ruling party  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 16 Feb 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/explainer-what-were-indias-electoral-bonds-and-how-did-they-power-modis-party/1969006/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters described unlimited anonymous donations and the BJP as the largest beneficiary. That is counterevidence to a welfare-first state, because it points to capture-prone, patronage-heavy politics.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.1, 2B.6

**Synthesis**
- **Best positive case:** Modi’s 2024 government did pursue real welfare through budgets, health systems, rural programs, farmer support, and some administrative modernization.
- **Best negative case:** too much of the political record still treated people instrumentally, through communal mobilization, selective transfer politics, and coercive handling of vulnerable populations.
- **Overall:** I would rate this as **mixed, leaning negative** for 6B.1. Welfare was a genuine governing objective, but not consistently the core purpose of rule.
